title: Quality Compounding
hook: Every great client I've landed came from work I was genuinely proud of. None came from good enough.
statement: Better work attracts better opportunities. But only when the right people can actually see it.
explainer: Excellent work nobody sees doesn't bring opportunity. Visible work that's just okay doesn't either. You need both, and quality is the part you control first.
sop: List the last 5 things you shipped or delivered.
Rate the Quality of each, 1 to 10, against your own best.
For anything under 8, name the corner you cut.
Rate your Visibility from 1 to 10. Who actually sees your best work?
Raise the floor on one recurring deliverable and show it off.
equation_example: Quality 9, Visibility 4. 9 × 4 = 36. Great work, but hardly anyone sees it. Higher means excellent work is reaching people who can act on it. Lower means it isn't excellent yet, or it's hidden.
question: Name one thing you've been letting slide as good enough that should be excellent.
closing_statement: Opportunity finds the standard, not the hustle.
caption:
Principle Nº 176: Quality Compounding

Every great client I've landed came from work I was genuinely proud of. None came from good enough.

Better work attracts better opportunities. But only when the right people can actually see it.

Your turn: Name one thing you've been letting slide as good enough that should be excellent.
